title: Video desk, Thu Nov 12 set: Earnings This Week (Nov 17-19), Explained (gap fill), AI This Week

general-counsel-agent.note: All ten checks on file after reviewing the three 9:16 review sheets, report.json spoken text, titles, captions and sources. Defamation screen: earnings dates and estimates come from Webull and Nvidia's own Oct 28 release; gap figures from Webull bars; each AI story is reported by three or four outlets dated within 14 days. No reason is given for any price move. The one person named, OpenAI's Adam Fry, is quoted only for a figure he gave publicly, attributed to OpenAI, with the caveat that the method isn't published. A same-week Nvidia leadership story was left out on purpose: it is still developing and includes unproven claims about a person. Nothing commits the owner; delivery is to the owner only. AI review, not legal advice.

advertising-consumer-protection-counsel.note: Every number traces to a saved raw response or a named source: earnings dates, quarters and consensus estimates to raw/get_stock_earnings_calendar_*.json; Nvidia's Nov 17 date and call time to its Oct 28 release; last quarter's $96.2B vs $92.2B to the NVDA earnings record; QQQ, SPY and AMD gaps, fill bars, lows and closes to the saved daily and 5-minute bars. AI stories: the ChatGPT one-fifth figure is presented as OpenAI's own claim; GDPx's 206 tasks, 11 fields and 12% top score match SemiAnalysis; the Anthropic $70 to $78 range is called expected with the final price not set. The AI caption discloses that the studio uses Anthropic's Claude and that the video isn't sponsored. Outros say 'Follow for more' with no schedule promise.

email-anti-spam-compliance-counsel.note: No commercial email. The delivery email goes to the owner only.

privacy-data-protection-counsel.note: No personal data. The only person named is a company executive speaking publicly in his job; no private person is named and the owner isn't named or shown.

copyright-fair-use-counsel.note: Visuals are drawn from data by the kit's renderer; the voice is Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0); music is synthesized per video by music.py; fonts are Inter, Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono (SIL OFL). News is stated in our own words with outlets credited; no quotes beyond a short figure, no logos, footage, screenshots or third-party images.

trademark-brand-clearance-counsel.note: Nvidia, Walmart, TJX, Palo Alto Networks, Intuit, QQQ, SPY, AMD, OpenAI, ChatGPT, Google, SemiAnalysis, GDPx, Anthropic, Claude, Nasdaq and Webull are named only to refer to them (nominative use); no logos, nothing suggests endorsement. Series names are generic. Hashtags are generic. No USPTO search needed: no new brand or series name.

financial-content-compliance-counsel.note: 'Educational only. Not financial advice.' is on screen at the end of all three videos and in all three captions. No buy or sell calls, no targets, no predictions of beats or misses; the earnings video says 'No predictions here.' The gap video says a gap alone doesn't tell you whether it fills and gives no reason for any move. The IPO item states the expected range and that the price isn't final, with no suggestion to buy; the caption discloses the studio's use of Claude.

platform-terms-policy-counsel.note: Synthetic TTS narration over data charts and text cards; no realistic depiction of real people or events. Meta asks for a label on AI-generated audio, so turn on 'AI info' on Instagram and Facebook. Titles match the content; the AI title frames the one-fifth figure as OpenAI's claim.

kids-content-coppa-counsel.note: General-audience content, not directed to children; no child shown, no child's data. Mark 'not made for kids' where a platform asks.

contracts-commercial-terms-counsel.note: No paid tools, licensed assets or third-party agreements. Webull data is read-only and used for commentary. No sponsorship from any company named; the studio's use of Claude is a normal paid subscription, not a deal.
